column4: Pixel-art game character sprites in exactly the same style as the reference image, a mid-1990s Build-engine game: the same coarse pixel size, the same limited palette, the same shading and the same dark outline. A character turnaround model sheet: five full-body views of one and the same man standing perfectly still and stiff, arms hanging dead straight, head bowed slightly, side by side in a single row, evenly spaced with clear magenta gaps between them, all exactly the same height and scale with the feet on one common baseline near the bottom edge: (1) seen straight from the front, (2) a three-quarter view from the front with the body turned toward the right edge of the image, (3) an exact side profile facing the right edge of the image, (4) a three-quarter view from behind, turned away toward the right edge of the image so the back and the right shoulder show, (5) seen straight from behind, the back of the head and the back of the clothes. Every figure is exactly the man in the reference image, with the same face, body, proportions, clothes and colours: the same bucket hat, round glasses, patterned short-sleeved shirt over a green shirt, jeans and shoes, no backpack. His mouth is gone: in its place a pale wet membrane of skin stretched tight and sewn shut down the middle with thick black crude stitches, yellow pus seeping between them; behind the glasses his eyes bulge, bloodshot, staring; his skin waxy, sagging and wet, the shirt soaked with dark stains down the front, his fingers far too long with filthy broken nails. Body horror, morbid and repulsive, cursed nightmare fuel, not sexual. Background must be flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere around and between the figures, no ground, no floor line, no shadows, no text, no labels, no numbers, no grid lines, no frames, no borders, no watermark.

Pixel-art texture for a 1990s Build-engine game, a tent wall seen from inside the tent, flat and straight on, filling the whole frame edge to edge, exactly the same canvas, colour, weave and pixel style as the reference image. From outside, a man's face and both his hands are pressed hard into the canvas so it stretches tight over them: in the fabric itself the shape of a bucket hat brim, round glasses, a nose and a chin, and the long fingers spread on either side, all made only of stretched canvas and its creases, lit faintly from behind by the night outside. No person visible, only the shape pushing in through the fabric. Chunky pixels, low saturation, gritty and eerie, no text, no border, no watermark.

The only change: in each round lens of his glasses a small sharp reflection of the person looking at him, a pale frightened face lit from below by a torch in their hand, the same tiny reflection in both lenses, curved by the glass. Body horror, morbid and repulsive, cursed nightmare fuel, not sexual. Flat pure magenta #FF00FF background only in the corners, no text.
